scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The Connection Lab
scenes.caption: Tara sketches the makers-fair room so a delivery trolley can reach a table. Neel carefully draws every decoration but leaves out the narrow entrance. The drawing resembles the room, yet it cannot answer the practical question of whether the trolley can pass through.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: What changed?
scenes.caption: Abstraction keeps details that matter to a purpose and leaves other details aside. For this route, the entrance width, trolley width, obstacles and destination matter. Wall colour does not determine whether the trolley fits. A useful model can be simple without losing the constraints that affect success.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Follow the evidence
scenes.caption: The teacher changes the job: now visitors need to find the art display. Labels and visible landmarks may become relevant, while trolley width may not. The team states the new goal before revising the map. There is no single perfect abstraction for every question about the same room.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Decide and explain
scenes.caption: The trolley must fit through the entrance and reach the delivery table. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Check the consequence
scenes.caption: Include entrance and trolley widths along with the route obstacles. Decorative accuracy cannot replace a constraint that decides whether the route works.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Investigate in the lab
scenes.caption: Investigate a model has a purpose, then relevant constraints, then revise the model. Test your plan, read feedback and try a changed case. Save evidence; explain one limitation.
